findings: F1 (P2): engine/reconcile_index.py commit()/_settle() re-observe the retained artifacts of every task integrate.sh merely examined, not only those it published, because engine/integrate.sh emits the historical-validation receipt before the 'status == accepted' test; for such a task a silent, event-less change racing the acknowledgement window has its content identity overwritten at commit and is then discoverable only via the event-stream backstop or the periodic canonical rediscovery, not via the next sweep.

F2 (P3): the commit() docstring ('never re-observe at acknowledgement time') and the _settle() docstring ('only what this transaction itself published') contradict the code, which does re-observe settled entries and settles examined rather than published tasks. docs/incremental-reconciliation.md states the real behaviour correctly, so the inconsistency is confined to the Python docstrings.

F3 (P3): packet.json attributes the command 'bash tests/test-incremental-reconcile.sh' to logRef .singular-evidence/green.log, but that log contains only the five-test tests/run.sh summary and no single-file output; the packet discloses this ('Included in the gate run recorded in green.log'), and green.log, regression.log and the host's gate-check.log are byte-identical (sha256 41fb103e...44e800), consistent with deterministic summary output.

F4 (P3): tests/test-incremental-reconcile.sh hardcodes /opt/homebrew/bin/bash and /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.12/bin/python3.12 with no fallback or skip guard. The pattern is pre-existing at base ada2f1d0785a and is extended by the new real-entrypoint section; the fixture will fail outright on any host without those exact paths.

rationale: Scope is clean and independently confirmed: the committed range ada2f1d0785a..de588048edb5 touches exactly the eight owned paths and no forbidden path; the host scope check and secret scan both passed. Branch, headSha (de588048edb5), treeSha and campaign binding in audit-verification.json match the packet, with sourceIntegrity verified and zero changed paths, so the evidence is bound to the exact candidate I reviewed. I reproduce the host gate classification exactly as not-rerun-evidence-verified and do not restate it as passed. Acceptance criteria are met on evidence read in the source rather than on packet assertions. AC-1: red-baseline.sh is a real differential reproducer against the base engine tree with concrete failure strings, and the fixture is extended in place (INCREMENTAL_ENGINE_HOME resolves the engine under test once, before the unit section) rather than forked into a parallel harness; the canonical-versus-indexed comparison over the pinned corpus compares the integrator's own skip/FAILED/INTEGRATED decisions including missing-branch, malformed and nonterminal packets. AC-2: _read_events consumes a persistent byte cursor under --max-events; _sweep advances an independent resumable frontier pass under separate directory, directory-entry and byte limits, and _hash_entry charges a full fixed block before reading it so the byte ceiling is real; tests assert entriesScanned and bytesHashed stay within declared limits. AC-3: the revisit bound is documented as ceil(remainingEntries/maxSweepEntries)+ceil(deferredBytes/maxSweepBytes)+1, reported per plan, and tested for non-starvation under continuous arrivals; silent same-size replacement, deletion, restoration and missing-to-present transitions are covered, with identity a digest over ordered block digests and size rather than mtime. AC-4: shared identity (target head, policy, campaign) and per-candidate identity (branch head including packed refs, commit/tree availability) are digested separately, so an unrelated local change dirties only its own entry while a true shared change invalidates the affected set with work still bounded. AC-5/AC-6: plan writes only a pending proposal; commit runs at the existing end-of-actuation boundary and only when the canonical scan exited 0; missing, corrupt, outdated-schema and forged indexes all fail open to full canonical discovery via _safe_plan, FORGED_KEYS are stripped and never honoured, integrate.sh ignores --dirty-tasks outside a reconcile cycle, and the index-disabled path is preserved and compared; the fixture exercises truncation, rotation, duplicate events, cursor discontinuity, index loss/corruption, forged entries and interruption before acknowledgement with exactly one gate run and one publication surviving. AC-7: diagnostics are deduplicated by (reason, dependency identity) with new/resolved transitions, and ops health exposes index health, backlog bytes, sweep pass, remaining work and pendingAcknowledgement while keeping authority discovery-only. AC-8: receipts are emitted at the real expensive boundaries inside the production integrator, and the second and third unchanged real --actuate cycles record zero historical validations and zero final authority checks, repeated over a complete sweep on a fixture with no eligible dispatch work. AC-9: the receipt separates sweep, rebuild, canonical and control-plane sections with platform and uncertainty fields, feeds TASK-1106's existing evaluator rather than a new service, and the test asserts the absence of savings/token/usd/threshold claims. AC-10/AC-11: documentation covers comparison, recovery, activation and fallback, and both docs and the packet's nextAction explicitly leave the fresh independent audit, the host-run exact-merged-tree integration gate and the complete canonical host suite open, claiming no B1 completion, runtime adoption or operational improvement, with TASK-1009 at 3a47a736 and the prior recovery records untouched. The four findings are non-blocking: F1 is a narrow residual race whose worst case is delayed, not permanent, concealment because periodic canonical rediscovery withdraws any selection and the event cursor is not advanced past the racing arrival; F2 through F4 are documentation and portability notes, and F4 is pre-existing at base. No P0 or P1 defect survived verification, so I accept on this evidence while recording F1-F4 as backlog.
